sysv86-kromite-kromite-memory-auto-skill.description: How to decide whether a just-completed piece of work is actually worth turning into a new SKILL.md, without being explicitly asked, and how to write it when it clears that bar. This is a high-bar, low-frequency skill — most tasks should NOT produce a new skill file. Use when a real, verified, non-trivial procedure has just paid off (worked, was checked, and would clearly save real effort if reused), or when the user says something like "remember this for next time" or "make this repeatable."

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-bounty.description: Practical playbook for finding and reporting real vulnerabilities in bug bounty and coordinated disclosure programs (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Intigriti, vendor VDPs). Use when the user wants to hunt for bugs against an authorized target, plan recon or attack-surface mapping, decide which vulnerability classes to test next, triage or verify a candidate finding, or write up a report. Covers a structured hunting workflow — attack-surface mapping, systematic vulnerability-class coverage, dedup-checking against public disclosures — plus the operational discipline that keeps findings valid and…

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-browser.description: Automate, test, or scrape the web from a coding agent that has no browser MCP server or browsing tool connected — CLI/local-runtime environments only. Use when the user asks to check a live page, fill a form, run an end-to-end test, scrape public data, take a screenshot of a running app, or verify frontend behavior in a real browser, and no MCP browser connector is available. Not needed when a browser MCP tool is already connected — use that instead.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-caveman.description: Ultra-terse response mode that cuts output tokens while preserving full technical accuracy. Use when the user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief", "cut the fluff", "less tokens", asks for shorter/leaner answers, or invokes /caveman. Also apply when the user repeatedly signals impatience with padded, hedged, or over-explained answers.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-ui-copy-paste.description: Disciplined workflow for taking a found UI reference, component, or code snippet (from ui-research, a screenshot, or a link the user pasted) and adapting it into the project correctly — instead of pasting it in wholesale. Use whenever inspiration or example code from outside the project is about to be integrated into it, or when the user pastes a component/snippet and asks to "use this" or "make it look like this."

sysv86-kromite-kromite-ui-fake-taste.description: Establish and record a concrete visual/design direction before building or restyling UI. Use at the start of any frontend, landing page, app UI, or design-system task where no design direction has been given yet, or when the user's aesthetic request is vague ("make it look modern/clean/premium"). Produces a TASTE.md the project can be built against and checked back on.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-github.description: Senior developer workflow for coding agents working in Git, GitHub, GitHub Actions, issues, pull requests, organizations, GitHub Projects, GitHub Marketplace, or new repositories. Use when editing code, reviewing diffs, staging files, preparing commits, publishing changes, triaging issues or PRs, touching CI workflows, creating repositories, operating across multiple GitHub organizations (your own or someone else's), managing Projects boards/items, publishing an Action to GitHub Marketplace, or operating in CLI/IDE-style development sessions. Enforces mandatory git checkpointing, explicit…

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-mcps.description: Install, configure, secure, and debug MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers in coding-agent CLIs and IDEs — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and similar tools. Use whenever the user wants to connect a new tool/service (database, issue tracker, Slack, GitHub, a custom API) via MCP, is debugging a server that won't connect or won't authenticate, is choosing between transports or scopes, or wants a team-shared vs. personal server setup. Goes beyond default install-and-forget: covers auth, security, scoping, and troubleshooting properly.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-research.description: Forces exhaustive web research and documentation reading before technical claims, version-specific answers, or code generation. Use whenever the user asks about library/framework/API versions, feature availability, current best practices, or anything where training-data knowledge could be stale or wrong. Trigger especially when the user mentions a version, release, or feature that seems to contradict internal knowledge — treat that as a signal to verify, not to correct the user from memory.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-scope-guard.description: Anti-overengineering discipline for high-autonomy coding models (Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and similar). Use for every code-writing, bug-fix, refactor, or architecture request. Blocks unrequested abstractions, "future-proofing" config, speculative error handling for unstated failure modes, unrelated refactors, and diffs bigger than the task needs. Also use when about to add self-check/verification instructions to a prompt or subagent brief — on this model generation that causes redundant re-verification loops instead of better output. Trigger on "fix this", "add a function", "refactor",…

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-strict.description: Strict, evidence-first task execution for precise and non-flattering answers. Use when the user wants analysis before interpretation, verification of provided text, images, code, screenshots, tests, benchmarks, or claims, hard factual critique, or a reusable standard for avoiding hallucination, weak conclusions, cherry-picking, and unverified assumptions.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-subagents.description: How to decide when to use subagents and how to configure and run them correctly in agentic coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex CLI, and similar tools). Use when the user asks about subagents, multi-agent workflows, parallel agents, delegating tasks to specialized helpers, or when a session's context is getting cluttered with search results, logs, or a long review pass that belongs in an isolated worker instead.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-system.description: Investigate the actual runtime environment — OS, shell, terminal/IDE/CLI host, hosting context (bare metal, VM, container, CI, cloud sandbox), and available tooling — and record it in a SYSTEM.md file so future sessions don't have to rediscover it. Use at the start of a new project or agent session when no SYSTEM.md exists yet, when the user asks what environment/system you're running in, or when something OS-specific (paths, shell syntax, package manager, line endings) is about to matter for the task.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-ui-ui-research.description: Research-first workflow for UI and frontend work — verifying current design-system specs, brand precedent, and up-to-date implementations of trend-driven visual effects (e.g. glassmorphism/liquid-glass, expressive shape systems, complex motion) before building. Use when implementing a named design system, matching an existing brand, or reproducing a current visual effect that needs verified, current technique rather than a remembered pattern that may be stale or under-detailed.

sysv86-kromite-kromite-dev-universal.description: Load and run several skills from this collection together for the rest of the session, via "/universal name1_name2_name3" (underscore-separated). Use whenever the user invokes /universal, asks to combine/stack multiple skills at once, or asks which skills can be run together.
